## What The Business Is

Rocket Lab is an end-to-end space company in Aerospace & Defense, spanning launch services, spacecraft manufacturing, satellite components/subsystems, and — if the pending Iridium deal closes — satellite network operations. Management framed the company in its May 8, 2026 Q1 call as one of few vertically integrated providers able to build, launch, and potentially operate space-based applications. In Q1 2026, Rocket Lab reported record quarterly revenue of **$200.3M**, GAAP gross margin of **38.2%**, and backlog of about **$2.2B**, with Space Systems representing the larger share of revenue and backlog. ([investors.rocketlabcorp.com](https://investors.rocketlabcorp.com/node/12416/pdf?utm_source=openai))

## What It Does

Rocket Lab’s launch business includes **Electron** for dedicated small-satellite orbital launches, **HASTE** for suborbital hypersonic and missile-defense test missions, and **Neutron**, a medium-lift reusable rocket under development for constellation and national-security missions. Its Space Systems business builds satellite buses, spacecraft, solar products, optical systems, propulsion, mechanisms, and other components for commercial, civil, and defense customers. Recent acquisitions have expanded this stack: Mynaric added laser optical communications terminals, while Motiv Space Systems is intended to add robotics, motion-control systems, and spacecraft mechanisms. ([rocketlabcorp.com](https://rocketlabcorp.com/updates/rocket-lab-completes-mynaric-acquisition-adding-laser-optical-communications-to-growing-space-systems-portfolio/?utm_source=openai))

## Recent Highlights (Positive)

Rocket Lab’s cadence and defense positioning improved during the last 90 days. On June 22, 2026, it said it launched the U.S. Space Force **VICTUS HAZE** mission after receiving notice-to-launch only **16 hours and 42 minutes** before liftoff, setting a responsive-space record and deploying Rocket Lab’s own Pioneer spacecraft. ([globenewswire.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/06/22/3315647/0/en/rocket-lab-shatters-responsive-space-record-launches-u-s-space-force-victus-haze-mission-in-16-hours-42-minutes.html?utm_source=openai))

Commercial launch activity also continued: Rocket Lab’s launch manifest page lists the **“Ten Owl of Ten”** Electron mission for Synspective on **June 27, 2026**, and Space.com reported that the mission successfully deployed a Japanese Earth-observation radar satellite, making it Rocket Lab’s 12th launch of 2026 at that point. ([rocketlabcorp.com](https://rocketlabcorp.com/missions/launches/?utm_source=openai))

Contract momentum was another key positive. In May, Rocket Lab announced its largest launch contract to date: **five dedicated Neutron flights plus three Electron launches** for a confidential customer, taking the company’s launch manifest above 70 missions and backlog above $2.2B. That followed a Q1 HASTE block buy described by the company as a **$190M** order for 20 hypersonic test flights. ([rocketlabcorp.com](https://rocketlabcorp.com/updates/rocket-labs-biggest-launch-deal-yet-confidential-customer-books-multiple-neutron-and-electron-launches/?utm_source=openai))

Strategically, Rocket Lab announced on June 29, 2026 that it would acquire **Iridium Communications** for about **$8B** in cash and stock, adding an operating satellite network, L-band spectrum, and recurring communications revenue if completed. The company expects closing in mid-2027, subject to approvals. ([investors.rocketlabcorp.com](https://investors.rocketlabcorp.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rocket-lab-acquire-iridium-historic-deal-creating-fully?utm_source=openai))

## Recent Highlights (Negative)

The Iridium deal is transformative but adds material execution, financing, and approval risk. Rocket Lab said the cash portion would be funded with balance-sheet cash plus additional debt and equity sources, and reports noted a **$3.6B bridge loan facility** commitment; closing still requires Iridium shareholder approval, regulatory clearances, and other customary conditions. ([govconwire.com](https://www.govconwire.com/articles/rocket-lab-iridium-8b-cash-stock-acquisition?utm_source=openai))

Neutron remains a major program risk. Management said in Q1 that the first launch was still targeted for later in 2026, but prior company materials had already pushed the first launch target to **Q4 2026** after a Stage 1 tank test failure, underscoring schedule and technical uncertainty for a vehicle central to medium-lift growth. ([nasdaq.com](https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/rocket-lab-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial-results-posts-record?utm_source=openai))

Launch execution can remain lumpy. Space.com reported that Rocket Lab aborted the **“The Grain Goddess Provides”** Electron launch attempt for iQPS at the last second on June 30, 2026; while such aborts can be normal safety behavior, they highlight operational sensitivity in a high-cadence launch model. ([space.com](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/rocket-lab-launch-iqps-radar-satellite-grain-goddess-provides?utm_source=openai))

Financially, the company is still scaling through heavy investment and acquisitions. Q1 GAAP operating expenses were **$132.5M**, above guidance, while management cited continued Neutron investment and integration of acquisitions; this leaves profitability dependent on backlog conversion, launch cadence, margin retention, and integration performance. ([fool.com](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/08/rocket-lab-rklb-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/?utm_source=openai))

## Transcript Read — Long Case

- Record Q1 revenue of $200.3M, +63.5% YoY, above guidance
- Record backlog of ~$2.2B, +20% QoQ, +108% YoY
- 31 new Electron/HASTE launches booked in Q1, more than all of 2025
- 5-flight Neutron deal with confidential customer, largest contract ever
- HASTE 20-launch $190M order from Kratos/DoD, largest single order in program
- Anduril partnership for 3 HASTE launches, expanding defense applications
- Selected with Raytheon for Space-Based Interceptor program under Golden Dome
- Motiv acquisition brings in-house robotic and mechanism capabilities, further vertical integration
- Electric propulsion system GÁ unveiled with 200-unit production line ready
- Neutron development on track for first launch by end of 2026; test campaigns progressing
- Cash and liquidity over $2B providing flexibility
- Revenue guidance for Q2: $225-240M, 16% QoQ growth at midpoint

Rationale: Record backlog (+108% YoY), strong demand across Electron, HASTE, and Neutron with a confidential 5-flight Neutron deal (largest in history), accelerating vertical integration (Motiv acquisition, electric propulsion), SBI program win with Raytheon, and rapid Neutron progress indicating positive future revisions.

## Bull Case

Record Q1 revenue ($200.3M, +63.5% YoY), backlog +108% YoY to ~$2.2B, and defense momentum (VICTUS HAZE responsive-launch record, SBI/Golden Dome selection with Raytheon, $190M HASTE block buy) support durable 40-60% top-line growth. A successful Neutron debut by year-end 2026 would unlock the medium-lift market and validate the pre-flight 5-launch contract. The Iridium acquisition, if closed, adds ~$800M+ of recurring communications revenue, L-band spectrum, and positive operating cash flow — transforming RKLB into a vertically integrated build-launch-operate platform. Liquidity of $2B+ funds the ramp.

## Bear Case

The stock trades at ~69x TTM revenue with negative FCF (-$315.6M TTM) that is *widening*, not narrowing — Q1 FCF was -$77.4M and guidance implies continued heavy burn. Q2 gross margin guides down (33-35% GAAP vs 38.2%), EBITDA losses widen, and opex climbs. Neutron's first launch is binary and has already slipped once (tank test failure). The $8B Iridium deal adds a $3.6B bridge loan, equity issuance/dilution, regulatory risk, and a mid-2027 close — meaning 12 months of deal overhang with none of the accretion. At a $48B market cap, Neutron success and Iridium synergies look substantially pre-priced.

## Multiple Re-Rating

- **Current implied multiple:** $47,201M EV / -$315.6M TTM FCF = **-149.6x** (optical, negative-FCF multiple)
- **12-month forward multiple:** **-115x** applied to forward FCF of ~-$380M
- **Direction:** **CONTRACT** (EV compresses ~7-8% while burn widens; the negative multiple moves toward zero in magnitude)
- **Drivers:** (1) The two major catalysts — Neutron first flight and the Iridium announcement — are largely priced at 69x sales; even a successful Neutron launch delivers "as expected" rather than upside. (2) FCF burn deepens on Neutron ramp, Mynaric/Motiv integration, and Iridium deal costs/bridge interest, pressuring the "story premium" as the market demands a visible path to breakeven. (3) Dilution/financing overhang from the cash-and-stock Iridium structure caps EV expansion; a $47B EV on <$1B revenue leaves no room for multiple expansion even in a supportive rate regime.

## Logic

1. **Forward FCF:** TTM FCF is -$315.6M and worsening (vs -$177M a year ago). With Neutron capex peaking into first launch, acquisition integration, and Iridium transaction costs, I forecast 12-month forward FCF of **-$380M**. Revenue growth (~$950M-1B forward) helps, but capex and opex growth outpace gross profit near term.
2. **Applied multiple:** Current optical multiple is -149.6x. I apply **-115x** — a contraction reflecting priced-in catalysts, deal overhang, and deeper burn.
3. **Forward EV:** -$380M × -115 = **$43,700M**.
4. **EV → Market cap bridge:** Current market cap ($48,273.6M) exceeds EV ($47,201.2M) by **+$1,072.4M** (net cash). Applying the same gap: $43,700M + $1,072M = **~$44,772M**.

Net: a ~7% pullback in market cap over 12 months as the market digests Iridium financing and demands proof of FCF inflection post-Neutron.

## Bull Case
Rocket Lab is executing across every vector: record Q1 revenue of $200.3M (+63.5% YoY), backlog of ~$2.2B (+108% YoY), the largest launch contract in company history (5 Neutron + 3 Electron flights), a $190M HASTE block buy, and a Golden Dome/SBI selection with Raytheon. The VICTUS HAZE responsive-launch record cements its defense credibility. A successful Neutron first flight by end-2026 unlocks the medium-lift market, and the pending $8B Iridium acquisition would add recurring communications revenue, L-band spectrum, and — critically — genuinely positive FCF to a business currently in heavy investment mode. Vertical integration (Mynaric, Motiv, propulsion) deepens the moat. With >$2B liquidity, the company can fund the Neutron capex wave.

## Bear Case
The stock trades at ~$48B market cap on $680M TTM revenue (~70x sales) with deepening cash burn: TTM FCF has worsened from -$137M (2024) to -$178M (2025) to -$316M today, and Q2 guidance shows sequential gross-margin compression (GAAP 33-35% vs 38.2%) and a widening EBITDA loss. Neutron's first launch is a binary event already pushed once after a tank test failure. The Iridium deal adds a $3.6B bridge loan, equity dilution, regulatory risk, and integration complexity — arguably a signal that organic growth alone can't justify the multiple. Nearly every 2026 catalyst (Neutron, defense wins, Iridium) has been announced and celebrated; the market cap has expanded far above its 3-year mean of ~$16.3B, leaving little room for disappointment.

## Multiple Re-Rating
- **Current implied multiple:** $47,201M EV / -$315.6M TTM FCF = **-149.6x** (negative FCF makes the optical multiple meaningless; the real anchor is ~70x EV/sales — extreme even for a story stock)
- **12-month forward multiple:** **-112x** on forward FCF of -$350M, implying forward EV of ~$39.2B (~17% EV compression)
- **Direction:** **CONTRACT** — the market pays materially less per dollar of the forward story, even though the negative multiple mathematically moves toward zero as burn deepens
- **Top drivers:** (1) Catalysts are substantially pre-priced — Neutron demand, defense wins, and the Iridium deal are all announced; even a successful Neutron debut is largely in the stock. (2) Dilution and financing overhang — the $8B Iridium deal requires new equity and a $3.6B bridge, capping per-share upside. (3) FCF trajectory deteriorates before it improves — burn widens through the Neutron capex wave and acquisition integration, which the market tolerated during the melt-up but will discount as the second derivative of revenue growth decelerates off a $2.2B backlog base.

## Logic
1. **Forward FCF:** Burn has roughly doubled year-over-year each year (-$137M → -$178M → -$316M). Neutron capex peaks into first launch, Mynaric/Motiv integration drags margins, and Q2 EBITDA loss widens sequentially. Some offset from revenue scaling toward a ~$1B run-rate and backlog conversion. I estimate 12-month forward TTM FCF of **-$350M** (continued deep burn, but decelerating rate of deterioration).
2. **Applied multiple:** I forecast EV compression from $47.2B to ~$39.2B as the priced-in catalyst stack de-rates post-Neutron-debut and Iridium dilution crystallizes. That maps to an applied EV/FCF of **-112x** (= $39,200M / -$350M).
3. **Forward EV:** -112 × -350 = **$39,200M**
4. **EV → Market cap bridge:** Current gap = MC - EV = $48,273.6M - $47,201.2M = **+$1,072.4M** (net cash position). Forward MC = $39,200M + $1,072M ≈ **$40,272M**.
